summary:
Public Law 118-235, cited as the "Holcombe Rucker Park National Commemorative Site Act" (54 U.S.C. 320101 note), designates Holcombe Rucker Park in Harlem, New York, as the "Holcombe Rucker Park National Commemorative Site." 

Section 2(b)(1) authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to enter into cooperative agreements with appropriate public or private entities, including the Mayor of New York City or the Mayor's designee, for interpretive and educational purposes related to the Commemorative Site. Such purposes include installing a plaque, interpretive exhibit, or other marker, subject to the condition precedent of the written consent of the property owner, to memorialize Holcombe Rucker and recognize the park's historic role in the development of basketball and its players.

Section 2(b)(2) expressly provides that the Commemorative Site shall not constitute a unit of the National Park System. 

Section 2(b)(3) imposes specific limitations on the Act's effect. Subparagraph (A) provides that the Act does not authorize the Secretary to interfere with private property rights or any local zoning ordinance or land use plan of the State of New York or its political subdivisions, nor does it prohibit actions otherwise permissible by the property owner. Subparagraph (B) stipulates that the Act does not affect the administration of the park by New York City or the State of New York. Subparagraph (C) prohibits the Secretary from acquiring land or interests in land through condemnation or otherwise. 

The Act was approved on January 4, 2025, and contains no appropriations.
